faqs.a:
(a)
For inspection purposes and performance of routine maintenance, authorized employees
               of the city shall be allowed free access at reasonable hours to any building or premises
               to which city water or sewer service, or both, are provided. All such employees carry
               an identification card signed by the city manager and containing a picture of the
               employee. Unless such employee possesses such an identification card, the employee
               need not be admitted to the building or premises.
(b)
The city has the right of ingress and egress to utility easements and rights-of-way
               containing city water or service lines, or both, at any time for the purpose of making
               repairs and making inspections to determine if repairs are needed.
(c)
Except as may be authorized by revocable permit issued by the city, no permanent obstruction,
               including but not limited to buildings, patios, sheds, trees, or fences may be located
               in a right-of-way or utility easement. When it is necessary for the city to accomplish
               maintenance or repair of any utility that is located within a right-of-way or utility
               easement, the city shall accomplish the work in a manner which minimizes disruption
               of the landscape, and shall replace landscape damaged by the work. All costs associated
               with moving or removing a permanent obstruction that encroaches on or is located in
               a right-of-way or easement will be borne by the owner of the obstruction.
(Code 1981, § 33-48; Ord. No. 2574, § 1, 11-21-1988; Ord. No. 2671, § 12, 10-16-1989;
               Ord. No. 2931, § 6, 10-19-1992)
